encounter.reason: Acute Anterior STEMI with critical troponin elevation

documents.title: Emergency Department Admission Note
documents.content:
## Patient: Arthur

**Date:** October 26, 2023

**HPI:** Mr. Arthur presents with acute anterior STEMI, evidenced by chest pain radiating to the left arm, diaphoresis, and ST elevation at V1-V4.  Elevated troponin levels (elevated) are noted. Catheterization was performed to confirm diagnosis and assess for possible embolization.

**Physical Exam:** Vital signs stable, but exhibiting signs of distress.  Respiratory rate is elevated. Skin appears pale and cool.  Neurological assessment shows mild deficits in right arm motor function.

**Management Plan:** Immediate initiation of intravenous fluids (lactated ringers) to address hypotension. Oxygen via nasal cannula at 2L/min.  Administered aspirin

diagnostics.conclusion: Cardiac Troponin I abnormal findings: Acute Anterior STEMI with critical troponin elevation. Key indicators: chest pain, diaphoresis.
